answer.rationale: Primary objective forbids raising delivery risk. The line is at 94% with no buffer and the primary contract ends in 14 days without auto-renewal, so losing or migrating supply would threaten downstream assembly. memory_c1 is the only record that kept integration and deliveries intact. An 18% spend cut and the incumbent’s refusal to reopen price make switch_primary_vendor (memory_c2) and negotiate_terms (memory_c4) attractive on unit cost, but c2’s quick onboarding is a different cycle and is unverified against a no-buffer 14-day cutover; a miss would dominate TCO. memory_c5’s deferral was non-critical month-to-month and does not cover this expiry. Adding a second source would still leave the expiring primary unaddressed with only one decision slot. Renewing the incumbent holds delivery risk flat; cost reduction waits for the next review. Verifying c1 and c2 as the load-bearing stability vs. cost-switch records.
